 Wouter Vrancken bemaoned yet more injuries before and during Heart of Midlothian ’s defeat to Trabzonspor.
 It was an improved performance from the Tynecastle outfit after their trashing at the weekend but they succumbed to a 2-0 defeat at Papara Park on Thursday night.
 Hearts are well into double figures when it comes to the number of players who have picked up injuries this season and they were dealt a huge blow when Harry Milne was ruled out with a suspected ACL issue, although the full extent won’t be known until he is back in Scotland and has it scanned.
 It went from bad to worse for Vrancken when Christian Borchgrevink pulled up in the first half with what appeared to be a hamstring injury.
 “Yeah, it was his hamstring. So, like he said himself: when it rains, it pours.
 “It's a bit like this at this moment. We have to manage it properly and try to get the best out of everybody. 
 “I hope to see that the guys out of position also, put everything in there, and do everything for the team, to help the team in these moments. So I'm happy to see this.”
 And Harry was unlucky because there was no fatigue because he didn't play in the last game.
 “It was not a contact, not a duel, not a crazy move or something. He injured his knee, so we have to see what the scans will say."
 With Milne unavailable and Stephen Kingsley left on the bench to manage his minutes, it meant Rogers Mato had to play at left-back against Trabzonspor’s Mo Salah and he acquitted himself well.
 Jordi Altena or Borchgrevink were options there from the start but Vrancken needed the Dutchman in midfield because of the ongoing injury crisis in midfield.
 Vrancken was delighted with both of their performances.
 "Mato is from the offensive players and I couldn't put a defender there, so we had to play an offensive player there. 
 "With his speed against Salah, it was a plus. And I know that in one-v-one situations he is difficult to pass when he's focusing on it. He showed it today. 
 “You can think about it as long as you won before the game. When Salah scores two times, three times today, then you say, well, that your decision was shit. 
 “But at the end of the day, you have to make some decisions like this, and it worked well. 
 “And when you see him, like I said, he played not against anybody, he played against Mo Salah and kept him out of the game. So a really great performance.
 “He was against one of the best players in Europe in this position. Also Jordi [Altena], out of position, played a really great game. So I'm really happy about the performance, and I'm just happy that there was no result.”
 In fact, Vrancken was pleased with the performance overall, despite the defeat.
 There were fear the multi-million-pound Trabzonspor could rack up the goals in a similar manner to how Celtic or Benfica have against Hearts this season.

 But the visitors battled well, kept their opponents quiet for large parts of the game and weren’t far away from taking the lead early in the game when Malachi Fagan-Walcott hit the post with a header.
 “In the dressing room, I said to them how proud I am today about their performance,” said Vrancken. 
 “When you lose, you always have this negative feeling, being a sportsman, but knowing where it comes from from the weekend, and all the injury stuff. 
 "We have only one midfielder left, six injured, so I have to say that you can't put your foot next to this team of Trabzonspor who spent a lot of money in the summer and even got a Mo Salah on a free transfer. So then you know what quality they have.
 “So I'm really proud of the performance from them, and then for me, they bounced back from the weekend, for sure, performance-wise. 
 "It's just a pity that we couldn't have the result because I think we didn't give too much away. The goals, we could prevent them, of course.
 “It's a shame that we have the penalty there, and we had to take our moments there. There were a few moments. Also, the clearest moment was the header from Malachi on the post.
 “When you want to win those top games in Europe, you have to take those moments.
 “It's very important this performance, to go to the next one to show that we can bounce back performance-wise. And hopefully it will give us confidence towards the weekend. We saw again guts on the ball, you saw people being brave in defence and one-v-ones against really top players. 
 "So it also has to give confidence towards the weekend."
